question: ap1
prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Transient stimulus with long-term chromatin accessibility tracking
ideas.description: Expose cells to a defined, brief AP-1-activating stimulus (e.g., TPA, injury, or cytokine), then perform ATAC-seq/CUT&RUN for AP-1 (FOS/JUN) and H3K27ac at time points from hours to weeks after the stimulus is removed. Persistent AP-1-motif-enriched accessible regions after the signal has decayed would indicate a memory state, and their re-engagement could be compared with naive cells.

ideas.title: Acute AP-1 degradation during the memory phase
ideas.description: Use degron-tagged (dTAG/AID) or dominant-negative (A-FOS) AP-1 to remove function either during the priming stimulus or only after it, and then measure maintenance of accessibility and transcriptional responses on re-stimulation. If depletion during priming but not after prevents memory, AP-1 is needed for establishment. If depletion after priming erases memory, it is needed for maintenance.

ideas.title: Secondary-challenge transcriptional response assay
ideas.description: Prime cells with a first stimulus, rest them, and then re-stimulate. Use RNA-seq, nascent transcription (PRO-seq) or single-cell readouts to quantify faster or stronger induction of AP-1 target genes versus unprimed controls. Test whether the enhanced response is gene-specific and tracks AP-1 binding sites, and whether it persists through cell divisions.

ideas.title: Single-cell multiome lineage tracing of memory inheritance
ideas.description: Combine single-cell RNA and ATAC-seq with clonal barcoding or live-cell imaging of AP-1 reporters (e.g., FOS–GFP) to test whether primed accessibility and AP-1 activity states are inherited by daughter cells. Comparing clonal sibling concordance with that of random cell pairs quantifies heritability and heterogeneity.

ideas.title: Causal site-specific perturbation of AP-1 motifs and pioneer activity
ideas.description: Use CRISPR base editing or dCas9-based tools to mutate or block AP-1 motifs at candidate memory enhancers. Alternatively, force AP-1 binding there with a synthetic recruiter in unprimed cells. Measure whether these changes alter retention of accessibility, histone marks and gene response, to separate AP-1 as the cause of memory from AP-1 as a marker. Pair this with BAF/chromatin remodeler inhibition to test the mechanism.
